---
title: "US - Baby Names - Solutions"
output: html_document
---

### Introduction:

We are going to use a subset of [US Baby Names](https://www.kaggle.com/kaggle/us-baby-names) from Kaggle.
In the file it will be names from 2004 until 2014

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
```

### Step 2. Import the dataset from this [address](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/master/06_Stats/US_Baby_Names/US_Baby_Names_right.csv).

### Step 3. Assign it to a variable called baby_names.

```{r}
# the same file is also included in this folder: read_csv("US_Baby_Names_right.csv")
baby_names <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/master/06_Stats/US_Baby_Names/US_Baby_Names_right.csv")
glimpse(baby_names)
```

### Step 4. See the first 10 entries

```{r}
head(baby_names, 10)
```

### Step 5. Delete the first (unnamed) column and 'Id'

```{r}
# the first column has no name in the file, so readr calls it "...1"
baby_names <- baby_names |> select(-1, -Id)
head(baby_names)
```

### Step 6. What year has the highest number of baby names in the dataset?

```{r}
baby_names |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(Count = sum(Count)) |>
  slice_max(Count, n = 1)
```

### Step 7. Are there more male or female names in the dataset?

```{r}
baby_names |> count(Gender)
```

### Step 8. Group the dataset by name and assign to names

```{r}
# group the data and sum only the Count column
names <- baby_names |>
  group_by(Name) |>
  summarise(Count = sum(Count))

# print the first 5 observations
head(names, 5)

# print the size of the dataset
dim(names)

# sort it from the biggest value to the smallest one
names |> arrange(desc(Count)) |> head()
```

### Step 9. How many different names exist in the dataset?

```{r}
# as we have already grouped by the name, all the names are unique already
nrow(names)
```

### Step 10. What is the name with most occurrences?

```{r}
names |> slice_max(Count, n = 1) |> pull(Name)

# OR

# names |> filter(Count == max(Count))
```

### Step 11. How many different names have the least occurrences?

```{r}
names |> filter(Count == min(Count)) |> nrow()
```

### Step 12. What is the median name occurrence?

```{r}
names |> filter(Count == median(Count))
```

### Step 13. What is the standard deviation of names?

```{r}
sd(names$Count)
```

### Step 14. Get a summary with the mean, min, max, std and quartiles.

```{r}
summary(names$Count)

names |>
  summarise(count = n(), mean = mean(Count), std = sd(Count), min = min(Count),
            `25%` = quantile(Count, 0.25), `50%` = median(Count),
            `75%` = quantile(Count, 0.75), max = max(Count))
```
